content.text:
I used all 3 merit measurements and submitted **index 175** (Fe 0.61, Ni 0.215, V 0.175). It had the highest photocurrent I measured, 7.7×10⁻⁷ A. I don't know how that compares with the best composition in the library. Only 3 of the 201 candidates were measured, and the part with more than about 50% Ni was never tested.

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 144 | 0.41 / 0.18 / 0.41 (close to FeVO₄) | 4.1×10⁻⁷ |
| 49 | 0.62 / 0.22 / 0.16 (highest Fe in the library) | 7.0×10⁻⁷ |
| 175 | 0.61 / 0.215 / 0.175 | 7.7×10⁻⁷ |

- **Pattern:** films with more iron gave more photocurrent than the FeVO₄-like film, so I put the last measurement next to index 49. Points 49 and 175 are almost the same composition, so the 10% gap between them is small evidence. The Fe-rich edge is the best area found, not a confirmed optimum.
- **Model inputs were weak:**
  - The phase list was too large to show, so I never saw which phase each ID belongs to. I looked up band gaps by guessing Materials Project IDs; two were valid.
  - Their predicted gaps (about 2.75 eV at the higher-accuracy HSE level) are below the 3.2 eV photon energy, which only suggests these phases absorb the light. I didn't run any stability calculations.
  - The Gaussian-process model had only one or two points, so its suggestions told me little. It proposed Fe-rich neighbours like index 79, which I didn't measure.
- **XRD:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are actually present is unknown.
